findings.title: Cleanup job ticker interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute without explanation
findings.body: The ticker driving ALL cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, user invites, short URLs, query history) was changed from `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10)` to `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1)`. This is a 10x increase in the frequency of every cleanup job, not just the annotation cleanup job this PR is meant to fix. The PR description only discusses splitting annotation cleanup queries to avoid MySQL deadlocks and says nothing about changing the cleanup cadence. This looks like an unrelated/unintentional change that will significantly increase database load for all cleanup jobs and could itself contribute to lock contention (the very problem this PR tries to solve), and should be reverted or explicitly justified.

findings.title: Normal, successful cleanup operations logged at Error level
findings.body: In CleanAnnotations (lines 534, 537, 554, 557) and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags (lines 576, 579), `r.log.Error(...)` is called on every batch iteration regardless of whether an error actually occurred (the `err` value logged is often nil, and these calls happen on the success path). Since this cleanup job runs continuously in the background, this will flood logs with Error-level entries during completely normal operation, which can trigger false alerts in monitoring/alerting systems that key off error-level logs and makes it harder to spot genuine failures. These should be logged at Debug/Info level, with only real failures logged as errors.

findings.title: Full ID list logged on every batch, which can be very large
findings.body: The log calls on lines 534, 554, and 576 include the full `ids` slice as a log field. Since the batch size (`AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize`) can be configured very large (the new test uses 32767), each cleanup iteration will serialize and emit a potentially huge list of integers into the logs on every batch, which adds unnecessary overhead and can bloat log storage, especially since (per the previous finding) these are logged unconditionally at Error level.

findings.title: fetch-then-delete split introduces a TOCTOU window not present with the previous atomic subquery DELETE
findings.body: CleanAnnotations/CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags now call fetchIDs and deleteByIDs as two separate WithDbSession calls (not wrapped in a shared transaction), whereas previously a single DELETE ... WHERE id IN (subquery) statement was atomic. Between the SELECT and subsequent DELETE, concurrently running cleanup instances (e.g. in a multi-instance Grafana deployment without a server lock around this specific call) or other writers could change which rows match, causing deleteByIDs to delete fewer/different rows than counted, so the reported 'affected' counts from CleanAnnotations/CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags can diverge from what was actually intended to be deleted. This behavior change is only partially acknowledged in a code comment ('may under-delete') but is not covered by any new test demonstrating the acceptable failure mode under concurrent access.
